manifest.name: The Parody World
manifest.author: WrestleCraft
manifest.description: Every company and wrestler here is a parody: a joke about the business and the people in it, with changed names and no real logos. Its history runs from 2020 to the day the game begins. Any resemblance is the point of the joke.
manifest.disclaimer: This is a work of parody. The companies and wrestlers in it are fictional and are not endorsed by, or affiliated with, any real promotion or person.

promotions.name: EWE
promotions.blurb: The upstart that stopped being an upstart. Owned by a football heir with a spreadsheet for every feeling, it books long, hard matches, signs everybody, and argues with the internet every Wednesday night.

promotions.name: WWC
promotions.blurb: The giant. Owned by a sports and entertainment conglomerate that counts everything twice, run by a former champion who swears the old days are over. Three brands, two stadiums a year, and more cameras than wrestlers.

promotions.name: OTPW
promotions.blurb: Japan's biggest company, which tours in long series of small shows that build to one night at the big dome. Strong style, long matches, and a summer tournament that ruins everybody's knees.

promotions.name: AYY
promotions.blurb: Mexico's loudest company: flying luchadores, clowns with chainsaws, and a summer spectacular in a bullring. Bought last year by the American giant, which has promised to change nothing and changed the lighting.

events.name: Fiesta en la Plaza de Toros

promotions.name: SUPERNOVA
promotions.blurb: The best women's wrestling company in the world, by its own count and most other people's. Idol singing, factions with colour schemes, and a summer league that runs longer than some marriages.

promotions.name: CALL
promotions.blurb: The oldest wrestling company in the world, nearly a hundred years old, running the same old arena every Friday since before television. Masks are sacred, the técnicos are good, the rudos are bad, and that is that.

promotions.name: TBA
promotions.blurb: The company that has changed its name, its network and its owner more often than its ring ropes. Always the comeback story, always one deal away from the big time, and always loved by the people who stayed.

promotions.name: WPW
promotions.blurb: The fed that grew out of PCW and took in everybody who ever signed up: four feds of history, one locker room, and a World title first held by a Shakespearean.

promotions.name: ARK
promotions.blurb: The company that sailed away from the old giant to build its own boat. Heavy chops, heavier kicks, and a fanbase that counts every elbow drop.

promotions.name: DDW
promotions.blurb: The indie that runs warehouses, bowling alleys and a parking lot in Atlantic City. Light tubes, thumbtacks and a crowd that throws its own chairs in. Everybody has wrestled here once, and most of them regret it.

workers.gimmick: A sad-eyed cowboy who drank his way out of the top spot, found himself in a field, and came back to win everything. He still apologises after every buckshot lariat.
workers.finisher_description: He springs off the top rope as his opponent stands, and clotheslines them out of their boots. Then he says sorry.

workers.gimmick: A video-game-loving genius who has had the best match of the year so often it is now in his contract. He nearly died, came back, and still flips like he is twenty-five.
workers.finisher_description: A fireman's carry lifted high and dropped into a sit-out driver.

workers.gimmick: A bleeding, grinning street fighter who has wrapped his own fists in things that are not tape. He runs a gang of believers and wants wrestling to hurt again.
workers.catchphrase: I came here to hurt. You came here to watch.
workers.finisher_description: A double underhook DDT, delivered after a twelve-hour shift.

workers.gimmick: A smooth, dangerous former champion who took the long way round to the top and sends everyone the bill for the trip.
workers.catchphrase: This is my neighbourhood. You're trespassing.
workers.finisher_description: He hoists his opponent into a pumphandle and drives them into his knee.

workers.gimmick: A rich, smirking Long Islander who knows he is better than you, and that you know it. He has a ring, a scarf and a lawyer for every occasion.
workers.finisher_description: A cradled tombstone piledriver, finished with a wave to the cheap seats.

workers.gimmick_category: Best Wrestler in the World (He Checked)
workers.gimmick: A Cockney daredevil who does things in the air that make doctors write letters. He calls his finishes by number and never runs out.
workers.finisher_description: A running elbow to the back of the head from out of a handspring.
workers.finisher_move: Handspring elbow to the back of the head

workers.gimmick: A Japanese legend who once made it rain money in arenas and now just makes it drizzle. He is unbearably smug and unbearably good.
workers.finisher_description: He spins his opponent by the wrist into a short-arm lariat that does not let go.

workers.gimmick: A painted skater who throws himself off things that are too high, onto things that are too hard. He climbed a real mountain to prove a point nobody had made.
workers.catchphrase: Nothing to lose. I already lost it.
workers.finisher_description: A falling senton off the top rope, feet first, eyes closed.

workers.gimmick: A sunglassed slacker who wrestles with his hands in his pockets and, somehow, wins. He has never been in a hurry and never will be.
workers.catchphrase: (He puts his hands in his pockets. That is the catchphrase.)
workers.finisher_description: A running punch thrown with his hands still almost in his pockets.

workers.gimmick: A smirking veteran who has betrayed every partner he ever had and now leads a family of people he insults.
workers.catchphrase: Respect your elders. Then step aside for them.
workers.finisher_description: A double-arm-trap twisting slam, the switch flipped off.

workers.gimmick: A Canadian legend who came back from a broken neck and a quiet retirement, to spear people he used to tag with.
workers.catchphrase: Rated PG-13. Parental guidance strongly suggested.
workers.finisher_description: A running tackle so hard it leaves a crater.

workers.gimmick_category: The Wizard of Twelve Thousand Words
workers.gimmick: A veteran who knows twelve thousand holds and has named all of them in a promo. He reinvents himself every year and keeps a list of everybody who did not notice.
workers.catchphrase: You just made the list. Of synonyms.
workers.finisher_description: A single-leg crab with a knee in the back, and a definition read aloud.

workers.gimmick: A precise, giant Swiss strongman who swings people round by the ankles and keeps perfect time while doing it.
workers.finisher_description: He spins his opponent by the ankles for as long as the crowd counts.

workers.gimmick: A clean-cut student of the mat who joined a gang, bought a leather jacket and now practises sneering in the mirror.
workers.catchphrase: I'm dangerous now. Ask my mum.
workers.finisher_description: A trapped-arm rear submission he learned in school.

workers.gimmick_category: The Nastiest Man in the Building
workers.gimmick: A small, sharp, angry Englishman who does not care if you like him, which you do not.
workers.finisher_description: A corkscrew senton from the top rope.

workers.gimmick: A huge Japanese athlete who moves like a cruiserweight and hits like a crane. He belongs to a family of people who think they own wrestling.
workers.finisher_description: A lifting knee to the jaw from a man who should not jump that high.

workers.gimmick_category: The Rising Star That Will Not Stop Rising
workers.gimmick: A lanky Australian prodigy who has had more great matches than birthdays.
workers.catchphrase: Watch the sky. I'm in it.
workers.finisher_description: A spinning tombstone into the mat.

workers.gimmick: A flyer who has never once taken the stairs when he could take the air instead.
workers.finisher_description: A springboard 630 senton, the full turn and a bit.

workers.gimmick: A thick-necked veteran who chokes people to sleep and then does a promo over them in a calm voice.
workers.finisher_description: A rear naked choke, delivered gently, until it isn't.

workers.gimmick: A giant who never says much and does not need to.
workers.finisher_description: A spinebuster from twice the usual height.

workers.gimmick: The silent, scowling son of a commentator, who throws people around like wet laundry and never smiles.
workers.finisher_description: A sleeper hold from behind, until the lights go out.

workers.gimmick: A Delaware farmer who wrestles like the roosters are watching and he owes them money.
workers.finisher_description: A shooting star elbow drop.

workers.gimmick: One half of a brother tag team who hold executive titles in the company and use them mostly to give themselves good matches.
workers.finisher_description: A thrust kick to the jaw, usually in a set of six.

workers.gimmick: The younger brother, who does more flips and fewer meetings.
workers.finisher_description: A springboard into a spinning kick, then a bow.

workers.gimmick: A muscle-bound legend who joined the business of hurting people for money and keeps the receipts in his biceps.
workers.catchphrase: Hurt is business. Business is booming.
workers.finisher_description: A full nelson that squeezes until a contract is signed.

workers.gimmick_category: The Gold Standard of Being Underrated
workers.gimmick: A veteran athlete who was told he was underrated for twenty years and decided to make everybody pay for it.
workers.finisher_description: A step-up knee to the face.

workers.gimmick: The manager of the hurting business, who sells you a deal you did not want and a beating you did not ask for.
workers.finisher_description: A running knee in the corner while his clients hold you.

workers.gimmick: A smirking New Zealander who once ruled the biggest faction in Japan and now leads a cowboy gang that sells hats.
workers.catchphrase: It's still real to me, mate.
workers.finisher_description: A spinning reverse STO.

workers.gimmick: A loud, sequinned brawler who talks too fast and punches too hard.
workers.catchphrase: Juiced up and nowhere to go!
workers.finisher_description: A left-handed punch from the top rope.

workers.gimmick: A rapper who writes a diss track about every opponent and occasionally wrestles them.
workers.catchphrase: Mic drop. Then a real drop.
workers.finisher_description: A top-rope elbow, then the microphone.

workers.gimmick: The likeable half of a rapping tag team, who makes the crowd do a hand gesture they all pretend not to love.
workers.finisher_description: A sit-out powerbomb from a fireman's carry.

workers.gimmick_category: Ageless Dad of the Tag Division
workers.gimmick: A legend in his sixties who manages younger men and still throws a better punch.
workers.catchphrase: Respect your elders. Especially this one.
workers.finisher_description: A fireman's carry into a jumping neckbreaker.

workers.gimmick: Half of a moustached tag team who think tag wrestling died in 1989 and are trying to dig it up.
workers.catchphrase: Old school. No school. Top guys.
workers.finisher_description: A double-team bulldog into a backbreaker.

workers.gimmick: The other half, who drives the van and fixes the trophies.
workers.catchphrase: We're the best. Ask anyone over sixty.
workers.finisher_description: A double-team neckbreaker.

workers.gimmick: A furious, pudgy, beloved brawler who cuts promos about his feelings and backfists the people who caused them.
workers.catchphrase: I'm tired. I'm angry. I'm here.
workers.finisher_description: A spinning backfist, the size of a bin lid.

workers.gimmick: A country veteran who breaks guitars over heads and then sells the strings.
workers.catchphrase: Ain't my first rodeo. Or second guitar.
workers.finisher_description: A falling facebuster, guitar optional.

workers.gimmick: A veteran in a gold bodysuit who has been wrestling since before most of the roster was born.
workers.finisher_description: A bulldog off the ropes.

workers.gimmick: A huge, bearded brawler who leads a gang of dark misfits and punches like a slammed door.
workers.finisher_description: A sit-out powerbomb from a cutter position.

workers.gimmick: A tiny Canadian who kicks faster than people can blink and once kicked his way through a whole tournament.
workers.finisher_description: A cradled, spinning driver after a flurry of kicks.

workers.gimmick: A high-flying athlete who leaps like he is late for a flight.
workers.finisher_description: A frog splash from the far corner.

workers.gimmick: A small, fast, shouting flyer who arrives at full speed and leaves at fuller speed.
workers.finisher_description: A frog splash from the top rope.

workers.gimmick: A daredevil who leaps off things for a living and has a stunt double for his stunt double.
workers.finisher_description: A corkscrew shooting star press.

workers.gimmick: A small, bearded technician who grows his own vegetables and lives in a van to save money. Semi-retired, he wrestles when the crowd chants for him, which is always.
workers.catchphrase: He points to the sky and the arena chants: YAY! YAY! YAY!
workers.finisher_description: He traps one arm with his legs, cranks the face back with a forearm, and asks politely whether they would like to tap before he composts them.

workers.gimmick: A masked Mexican athlete who can lift a man with one arm while doing a handstand, and often does.
workers.finisher_description: A handstand into a lifted bridging suplex.

workers.gimmick: A shining luchador who flips across the ring like a coin someone threw for luck.
workers.finisher_description: A springboard shooting star press.

workers.gimmick: A luchador who walks the top rope like it is a sidewalk and lands everything on the way down.
workers.finisher_description: A rope-walk into a moonsault.

workers.gimmick: A veteran who has broken more backs than a bad mattress and is proud of it.
workers.finisher_description: A backbreaker into a powerbomb.

workers.gimmick: A quiet technician who twists legs like pretzels and gets very annoyed at noise.
workers.finisher_description: A pretzel-shaped leg lock.

workers.gimmick_category: Promotions Boss of the Back Room
workers.gimmick: A huge, slow-talking brawler who runs a crew of hard men and tells them where to stand.
workers.finisher_description: A package piledriver.

workers.gimmick: A flamboyant veteran who comes to the ring with two attendants and a peacock feather and leaves with neither.
workers.finisher_description: A Northern lights suplex into a German.
workers.finisher_move: Northern lights into a German suplex

workers.gimmick_category: Teen Prodigy With a Mother Problem
workers.gimmick: A teenage wonder whose mother manages him, books him, and is on his match card more than he is.
workers.catchphrase: Ask my mum. She's in charge.
workers.finisher_description: A spinning cutter from the top rope.

workers.gimmick: A woman who speaks only in old movie lines, wears pearls to fight, and believes it is 1948. The crowd believes it too.
workers.finisher_description: A cradle piledriver, delivered with a fan's flutter.

workers.gimmick: A champion who calls herself the boss, wears a cape, and bills every opponent by the hour.
workers.catchphrase: The CEO-ish will see you now. Invoice to follow.
workers.finisher_description: A short-arm, cross-legged crossface that stays until the shares change hands.

workers.gimmick: A strongwoman from outer space, or Long Island, who lifts people like groceries and stares at the lights.
workers.catchphrase: Take me to your leader. Then I'll lift them.
workers.finisher_description: A lifting powerbomb with a spin.

workers.gimmick: A beaming, singing, laughing powerhouse who powerbombs people while smiling.
workers.finisher_description: A lifting sit-out powerbomb.

workers.gimmick: A tough, smoking English brawler who lariats people and buys them a drink afterwards.
workers.finisher_description: A running lariat to the back of the head.

workers.gimmick: A fiery Mexican legend who fights for her people and paints her face for battle.
workers.finisher_description: A Michinoku driver.

workers.gimmick: A former starlet's assistant who stole the act, the gown and the spotlight.
workers.finisher_description: A running knee to the face.

workers.gimmick: A singing, dancing Australian who writes a jingle for every match and loses most of them.
workers.finisher_description: A diving crossbody.

workers.gimmick: A cheerful flyer who wears blue from head to toe and kicks people in the head.
workers.finisher_description: A kick to the head that she calls a diagnosis.

workers.gimmick: A young goth who joined a dark family and speaks in riddles nobody asked for.
workers.finisher_description: A seated arm-trap lock.

workers.gimmick: A pretty, quiet assassin who chokes people out with a smile.
workers.finisher_description: A rear naked choke from behind.

workers.gimmick: A Japanese veteran who brings a kendo stick to the ring and uses it more politely than you'd think.
workers.finisher_description: A running knee strike.

workers.gimmick: A cold, precise technician who teaches the women's division a lesson every week and grades it harshly.
workers.finisher_description: A sit-out powerbomb into a leg lock.
workers.finisher_move: Sit-out powerbomb into a leg lock

workers.gimmick: An English punk from a wrestling family who came back from a career-ending injury and has never stopped talking about it.
workers.finisher_description: A DDT from the corner.

workers.gimmick: A hulking, roaring powerhouse who treats every match as a hunt.
workers.finisher_description: A lifting cutter into a powerbomb.

workers.gimmick: A teenager who started wrestling before she could drive and treats every crowd like detention.
workers.catchphrase: I'm grounded. You're on the ground.
workers.finisher_description: A swinging side slam.

workers.gimmick: A fallen goddess who has held the brand's title longer than some shows have been on the air, and expects to be worshipped for it.
workers.finisher_description: A lifting powerbomb into a neckbreaker.

workers.gimmick: A young flyer the brand has bet on, who keeps losing and keeps being loved.
workers.finisher_description: A running bulldog.

workers.gimmick_category: The Owner Who Reads the Comments
workers.gimmick: The football heir who owns the company, books the shows, reads every comment and answers some of them.
A smug Canadian manager who leads a family of the best wrestlers in the company and talks while they work.
workers.catchphrase: Don't look at me. Look at my family.

workers.gimmick: A masked commentator who knows every match in history and explains all of them, during the current one.
A veteran voice who has interviewed everybody, twice, and starts every answer with 'well'.
The legendary voice of a generation, who still calls the big ones and calls everybody 'partner'.
workers.catchphrase: Business is about to pick up, partner.

workers.gimmick: A face-painted legend who retired undefeated in his last company and now appears from the rafters on birthdays.
workers.catchphrase: One more time. Just once. Probably.
workers.finisher_description: A sharpshooter-shaped leg lock with a scorpion's sting.

workers.gimmick: The self-appointed Head of the Buffet, who demands to be thanked before every meal. He appears four times a year, takes all the credit, and leaves before the dishes.
workers.catchphrase: THANK me. Then pay the bill.
workers.finisher_description: A charging tackle through the midsection, finished with a breath-freshening point to the crowd.

workers.gimmick: An Austrian drill sergeant who believes wrestling is corporal punishment. He chops chests until they file a complaint and calls everyone 'small person', including taller people.
workers.finisher_description: A stiff, perfectly vertical powerbomb, followed by a lecture on posture.

workers.gimmick: A twin who left the family business to become the most cheered man in any arena. He has one word, and the crowd says it louder than he does.
workers.finisher_description: A frog splash off the top rope, preceded by three arm swings and a bounce.

workers.gimmick: A tattooed, soda-swilling rebel who once quit wrestling, then quit quitting. He talks for twenty minutes, insults everyone in the building, and somehow gets cheered for it.
workers.catchphrase: I'm the best in the building. Ask the building.
workers.finisher_description: He drapes his opponent over his shoulders and drops them face-first onto his rising knee, then tucks them in.

workers.gimmick: A man who dresses like a sofa at a royal wedding and calls himself a visionary. He leads a faction of young believers and never wears the same blazer twice.
workers.finisher_description: A running curb stomp, sold at full price.

workers.gimmick: A barking, bounding son of a famous family who tackles people for a warm-up. He has never once walked to the ring.
workers.finisher_description: He presses his opponent overhead and slams them, then issues a statement.

workers.gimmick: A giant from down under who splashes people from the top rope and then sits down to admire it.
workers.finisher_description: A full-weight senton from the top rope that registers on the local seismograph.

workers.gimmick: A legend's son who claims he did hard time for one weekend. He is booed out of every building and loves it.
workers.finisher_description: A frog splash his father taught him, done badly on purpose.

workers.gimmick: An Irishman who paints himself as a demon twice a year and keeps receipts the rest of it.
workers.finisher_description: A double foot stomp from the top rope, with a short window to pay.

workers.gimmick: A bearded, sweaty, emotional Canadian who has almost been world champion more times than anyone alive.
workers.finisher_description: A running kick to the face in the corner, still pending review.

workers.gimmick: A masked high flyer who breaks his opponent's arm and then asks the crowd to count the sides of his mask with him.
workers.finisher_description: An arm-trap package piledriver, followed by a theatrical arm snap.

workers.gimmick: The masked legend who has outlived three eras and his own son's respect. Still flies; lands slower.
workers.finisher_description: A springboard into the ropes and a dropkick through the middle, one number short of famous.

workers.gimmick: Once half of the happiest act in wrestling, now furious that nobody remembers their anniversary.
workers.finisher_description: A double-team boot and a seated senton.

workers.gimmick: Kojo Crown's partner, who plays a sad trombone at every opponent's misfortune.
workers.finisher_description: A top-rope elbow that ends in a slide whistle.

workers.gimmick: A pale Irishman who absorbs more punishment than any human in the company and keeps volunteering.
workers.finisher_description: A moonsault from the top rope that rarely hits anybody but himself.

workers.gimmick: A social media celebrity who wrestles like a natural and sells an energy drink between every move.
workers.finisher_description: A right hand with something shiny in it, then a sponsored pin.

workers.gimmick: A Bulgarian strongman who left, came back, and now crushes everybody without a holiday to celebrate it.
workers.finisher_description: A camel clutch so deep the opponent sees the back of their own knees.

workers.gimmick: A gothic Australian powerhouse who calls herself everyone's mother and bites if you disagree.
workers.catchphrase: Mother knows best. Mother hits hardest.
workers.finisher_description: A pumphandle lift into a sit-out powerbomb, with a card.

workers.gimmick: A tiny Japanese daredevil who moonsaults from places nobody has insured.
workers.catchphrase: The sky has no ceiling. My insurance does.
workers.finisher_description: A moonsault from the top rope with impossible hang time.

workers.gimmick: She keeps a list of everyone who ever wronged her and works through it alphabetically.
workers.finisher_description: A swinging reverse DDT, with late fees.

workers.gimmick: Vendetta Viv's very large best friend and accountant of violence.
workers.finisher_description: A powerbomb from a great height.

workers.gimmick: A fiery Irish legend who returned to remind everyone she runs this place, lunch break included.
workers.catchphrase: The Man-ager will see you now.
workers.finisher_description: A seated armbar so tight it hands back a receipt.

workers.gimmick: A young Irish technician with wings on her robe and a lot to prove.
workers.finisher_description: A top-rope elbow drop with a flutter.

workers.gimmick: A former hugger turned bitter turned hugger again, depending on the week.
workers.catchphrase: Hug it out or get out.
workers.finisher_description: A face-first driver into the mat, delivered with a hug.

workers.gimmick: The son of a dreaming legend who finished his story and then kept going, because the merchandise kept selling.
workers.finisher_description: He spins his opponent into a falling cutter, then points at the eagle on his shirt.

workers.gimmick: A kilted Scot who has been robbed of everything he ever held and talks about it constantly.
workers.finisher_description: A running jumping kick to the face, the size of a parking ticket.

workers.gimmick: A third-generation legend who strikes from out of nowhere, if his back allows it.
workers.finisher_description: A jumping cutter from out of nowhere. Nowhere is the corner.

workers.gimmick: A family enforcer who tried to take over the family and now leads a smaller one.
workers.finisher_description: A spike to the throat into a cobra hold, then a drop-off at the curb.
workers.finisher_move: Throat spike into a cobra hold

workers.gimmick: A huge man who moonsaults as if gravity owes him money.
workers.finisher_description: A moonsault from the top by a man who should not be able to do one.

workers.gimmick: A gravel-voiced veteran who became famous at forty and talks like a movie trailer.
workers.finisher_description: A running neckbreaker, delivered with a sunglasses toss.

workers.gimmick: A tall, spooky Puerto Rican who used to judge people and now just punishes them.
workers.finisher_description: A chokeslam that ends in a short homily.

workers.gimmick: A pudgy, ferocious Quebecer who swears at children and powerbombs men onto ring aprons.
workers.catchphrase: Fight me. Then buy me fries.
workers.finisher_description: A powerbomb onto the hardest part of the ring apron.

workers.gimmick: A slick high flyer who insists he is the main character, whoever that is.
workers.catchphrase: Main character energy. Side character results.
workers.finisher_description: A falling leg drop off the top rope with a long pause.

workers.ring_name: Ace of the Block Party Boys
workers.gimmick: Half of a tag team that turns every entrance into a block party.
workers.finisher_description: A frog splash with a party horn.

workers.ring_name: Deuce of the Block Party Boys
workers.gimmick: The other half, who carries the speakers.
workers.finisher_description: A spinning spinebuster.

workers.gimmick: A blonde former gymnast who believes the universe revolves around her, and the camera crew agrees.
workers.finisher_description: A moonsault with a full pause to pose.

workers.gimmick: A second-generation legend who has held every title, twice, and is offended you forgot.
workers.finisher_description: A forward somersault into a cutter, then a ten-minute strut.

workers.gimmick: A massive Samoan who sits on people and calls it a submission.
workers.catchphrase: Not like most people. Like most buildings.
workers.finisher_description: A leg drop off the top rope, followed by the building's structural engineer.

workers.gimmick: A sculpted powerhouse who looks like a superhero and does not need to tell you so.
workers.finisher_description: A rolling cutter so fast the replay needs a replay.

workers.gimmick: A sprinter with a braid that is legally a weapon.
workers.finisher_description: A fireman's carry into a facebuster.

workers.gimmick: A dancing veteran with glowing gear who turned nasty after twenty years of being nice.
workers.finisher_description: A running hip attack that leaves a mark you can see in the dark.

workers.gimmick: An Italian-Japanese bruiser who came from the best women's company in the world and wants everyone to know it.
workers.finisher_description: A northern lights suplex turned into a powerbomb.

workers.gimmick: A Canadian who demands to speak to the manager of every match she loses.
workers.catchphrase: I want to speak to the MANAGER.
workers.finisher_description: A double-arm DDT that leaves a form to fill in.

workers.gimmick: A smooth talker who changed his name to sound holier and his attitude to sound worse.
workers.finisher_description: A rolling cutter.

workers.gimmick: A tracksuited would-be mob boss who offers you a deal you would be wise to refuse.
workers.finisher_description: A spinebuster into the mat.

workers.gimmick: Half of a huggable tag team who apologise after every slam.
workers.finisher_description: A sit-out powerbomb.

workers.gimmick: The other half, who hugs the referee after every win.
workers.finisher_description: A bear hug into a slam.

workers.gimmick: The leader of a gang of influencers who film every beating for their followers.
workers.finisher_description: A running lariat.

workers.gimmick: A surfer who flips off the top rope like she is catching a wave.
workers.finisher_description: A springboard moonsault into a cutter.

workers.gimmick: A mixed martial artist who kicks like a door slamming and celebrates like a nightclub.
workers.finisher_description: A spinning back kick.

workers.gimmick: A bouncing super-fan who won a contract and still cannot believe it, loudly.
workers.finisher_description: A kimura lock.

workers.gimmick: A towering Nigerian who lifts men like luggage and wonders why the main roster has not called.
workers.finisher_description: A pop-up powerbomb from shoulder height.

workers.gimmick: A charismatic leaper the crowd sings about, whether he wants them to or not.
workers.finisher_description: A running kick to the face, delivered with a whistle.

workers.gimmick: The youngest man in the building, who flips like he has no bones and a lot of years left.
workers.finisher_description: A springboard cutter with a backflip on the way down.

workers.gimmick: A veteran who writes his own reviews and they are glowing.
workers.catchphrase: Read my book. I wrote it.
workers.finisher_description: A spinning driver into the mat, with an autograph.

workers.gimmick: A powerhouse who lifts men in her spare time and women in her main time.

workers.catchphrase: What'cha gonna do, little brother, when the bronze rubs off on YOU?
workers.finisher_description: He cups a hand to his ear for a full minute, rips his shirt in two, and drops a slow, flat leg across the throat.

workers.gimmick: A bald, foul-tempered roofer who hates authority, paperwork and anyone in a suit. He drinks room-temperature soda by the crate because the cooler is always broken.
workers.catchphrase: That's the bottom of the cooler, and it's WARM!
workers.finisher_description: A kick to the gut, a quarter turn and a jaw-jolting drop to the seat, then two cans of flat soda over the body.

workers.gimmick: The billionaire who used to own the giant, fires people on live television, rehires them after the commercial and makes them thank him. He was pushed out of his own company and wants it back.
workers.catchphrase: You're... FIRED. Effective after the merchandise sale.
workers.finisher_description: He swaggers to the ring like a broken windmill while three men in suits do the beating.

workers.gimmick: A towering funeral director for hire who has died eleven times and comes back every spring with a longer entrance.
workers.finisher_description: He turns his victim upside down, sits them into a piledriver with their arms crossed, rolls his own eyes back, and leaves a bill.
